title: Enums considered harmful: why Matt Pocock replaces TypeScript enums with as const objects
summary: Matt explains why TypeScript's enum keyword is a poor fit: it is not native JavaScript, produces surprising runtime objects, and makes TypeScript nominal. He recommends plain objects with `as const` plus a derived union type, which is more flexible and structurally typed, and says to flag enums in PRs without rejecting them.

principles.text: Prefer `as const` objects over enums; they fit TypeScript's structural typing and let callers pass plain values.
principles.quote: the thing that I do instead of using enums and I've seen this all over the place in open source application code is using a pojo a plain old JavaScript object that's just got this as const annotation on it

principles.text: Numeric enums compile to a reverse-mapped object, so Object.values returns surprising results at runtime.
principles.quote: it actually doesn't if we look at the transpiled JavaScript here then this log level actually ends up as a slightly different object

principles.text: Enums make TypeScript nominal, which clashes with the structural type system everywhere else.
principles.quote: for enums typescript becomes a nominal type system it cares about either whether it's a log level enum or a log level 2 2 enum here

principles.text: Avoid const enums, especially in library code, because they are dangerous when you don't control the compiler emitting them.
principles.quote: you should also never ever ever use them if you're inside Library code too because cons enums are really dangerous if you don't control the compiler that's emitting them

principles.text: `as const` objects can map semantic keys to richer values, and the type can be derived from keys or values, with less code than enums.
principles.quote: the other really cool thing about as const is it lets you be super flexible with the object that you create these keys in

principles.text: Be pragmatic in review: flag enums in PRs and suggest as const, but don't reject PRs just for using them.
principles.quote: I don't think you should reject PRS that have enums in but I do think you should try to monitor when they go into your code base and see if they're really necessary
